title: K-pop Stars Who Failed Auditions Before Making It Big - Stories of Persistence
excerpt: Jungkook was rejected by 7 agencies. Suzy failed JYP auditions 3 times. Discover the hidden rejection stories of today's top K-pop stars and their journeys of perseverance.
author: MEARROW Editorial Desk
content:
The crushing weight of hearing "maybe next time" instead of "congratulations" is something only those who've experienced it truly understand.

Every year, over 1 million aspiring idols walk into audition rooms carrying their K-pop dreams. And **99.9% of them are rejected**. But here's the surprising truth: many of today's Billboard-charting, stadium-touring K-pop superstars were once among those **rejected hopefuls**. Their stories prove that "NO" isn't the end—it's often **a new beginning**.

## Stars Who Shined After Countless Rejections

### Jungkook (BTS) - The Boy Who Overcame 7 Rejections

In 2011, a 14-year-old boy from Busan named Jeon Jungkook appeared on Mnet's audition program 'Superstar K3.' Though he didn't make it to the finals, his performance caught the attention of **7 different agencies**. However, most of them put contract discussions on hold, citing reasons like "too young" or "needs more development."

Jungkook ultimately chose Big Hit Entertainment (now HYBE), and after 2 years of training, debuted with BTS in 2013. A decade later, he made history by reaching **#1 on the Billboard Hot 100 with his solo single 'Seven'**. Industry insiders say the agencies that rejected him still regret their decision to this day.

### Suzy (Former miss A) - 3 JYP Rejections, Success on the 4th Try

The audition story of Suzy, known as "Korea's first love," is legendary. She was **rejected by JYP 3 consecutive times**. The feedback? "Lacking vocal ability" and "weak dance fundamentals." But Suzy refused to give up.

On her fourth attempt, she finally made it. Debuting with miss A in 2010, 'Bad Girl Good Girl' achieved **the fastest #1 in K-pop history** at the time. She later conquered the acting world with dramas like 'Dream High' and the film 'Architecture 101.' JYP later said in an interview, "Suzy's persistence is what made her."

## What Rejection Taught Them

Failure isn't just about setbacks. Many successful idols confess that "the experience of being rejected became the foundation for growth."

**Hwasa (MAMAMOO)** joined RBW Entertainment after being rejected by JYP. "It was really hard when I failed at JYP, but that experience made me stronger. I practiced with the determination that 'I will never fail again.'" She went on to become MAMAMOO's main vocalist, recognized as one of **Korea's greatest live performers**.

**Kang Daniel** shares a similar journey. After being rejected by several major agencies, he joined MMO Entertainment and appeared on 'Produce 101 Season 2,' where he earned the **highest number of votes in the show's history**, becoming Wanna One's center. "Every time I was rejected, I asked myself, 'What am I lacking?' That process shaped who I am."

_Behind countless rejections lies the sweat and tears shed alone in practice rooms_

## Success Stories After Changing Agencies

There are countless cases where rejection at one agency led to success at another. This demonstrates the importance of "finding the right fit."

### Minnie ((G)I-DLE) - From Thailand to Korea, Never Giving Up

Thai-born Minnie was **rejected multiple times by major agencies like JYP, YG, and SM**. Being a foreigner and having pronunciation issues were obstacles. But instead of giving up, she **enrolled in Korean language classes and focused intensively on pronunciation training**.

Eventually, Cube Entertainment recognized her potential, and she debuted as (G)I-DLE's main vocalist. In 2024, 'Queencard,' which she composed herself, **swept global charts** and established (G)I-DLE as a representative 4th generation girl group.

### RM (BTS) - "Idol Rappers Won't Sell"

BTS leader RM (Kim Namjoon) was already known as an underground rapper in high school, but major agencies rejected him, saying "idol rap has no market potential." He even received harsh criticism that "his visuals aren't suitable for an idol."

Only Big Hit's Bang Si-hyuk recognized his **musical talent and songwriting abilities**. The result? RM led BTS to **6 Billboard 200 #1 albums**, Grammy nominations, and even a UN speech, rewriting K-pop history.

## Late Bloomers Who Reached the Top

In the K-pop industry, "age" is a sensitive issue. Since most idols debut in their late teens to early twenties, being past your mid-twenties is often considered "too late." But some stars have shattered this prejudice.

**Jin (BTS)** debuted at 22, considered "old" for the time. But his **visuals and vocals** became core attractions of BTS, and his solo single 'The Astronaut' reached #51 on the Billboard Hot 100.

**Solar (MAMAMOO)** spent **7 years as a trainee**. After going through numerous agencies without landing a debut opportunity, she was already 24 when she finally debuted with MAMAMOO at RBW. Yet she led MAMAMOO to become a **representative 3rd generation girl group** and continues to thrive as a solo artist.

## MEARROW Data on 'Comeback Success Rates'

According to MEARROW (K-pop Talent Network) analysis, interesting patterns emerge.

**About 35% of currently active idols have auditioned for 2 or more agencies**, and **15% of these were rejected by 3 or more agencies**. Even more interesting: **idols with retry experience have an average career span 1.4 times longer**.

This is attributed to the stronger **resilience** and **goal orientation** of idols who have experienced rejection. The experience of overcoming failure becomes the driving force to persevere through tough times after debut.

Top-ranked agencies on MEARROW are aware of this. Recently, there's a growing trend of viewing **"retriers" more favorably than "first-time passers"** in auditions.

## Conclusion: Today's Rejection Builds Tomorrow's Success

If you're reading this after a recent audition rejection, remember:

**Jungkook was rejected 7 times. Suzy failed 3 times. Hwasa didn't make it at JYP.** But where are they now? Shining at the top of the world stage.

Rejection doesn't mean "you can't do it"—it might mean **"this isn't your place."** Somewhere out there is an agency that's right for you, someone who will recognize your potential.

**Don't give up. Try again. K-pop history has been written by those who refused to quit.**

MEARROW supports your journey. 🌟
